chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When one of you fasts the three days of the month, let him not argue with anyone, nor act foolishly, nor hasten to oaths and swearing by Allah. And if someone acts foolishly towards him, let him bear it patiently."

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: The three days (referring to the 13th, 14th, and 15th of the lunar month)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for a Shia Muslim during the three white days of fasting?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical discipline of fasting during the Ayyam al-Beed (13th, 14th, and 15th of the lunar month) to spiritual refinement, specifically warning against hasty oaths and maintaining composure when others act foolishly. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *zuhd* (asceticism) as integral components of fasting, extending its benefits beyond abstention from food to the purification of the tongue and character.
